unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγοντες ("saying") is represented only by the colon before the quotation.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek has the participle εὐλογημένος alone.

19:39.sourceText: καί τινες τῶν Φαρισαίων ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν Διδάσκαλε, ἐπιτίμησον τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου.
19:39.targetText: But some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, rebuke Your disciples!”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

19:40.sourceText: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Λέγω ὑμῖν ἐὰν οὗτοι σιωπήσουσιν, οἱ λίθοι κράξουσιν.
19:40.targetText: “I tell you,” He answered, “if they remain silent, the very stones will cry out.”

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν ("answering said") is rendered answered.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds emphasis; the Greek has only the article.

19:41.sourceText: Καὶ ὡς ἤγγισεν, ἰδὼν τὴν πόλιν ἔκλαυσεν ἐπ’ αὐτήν,
19:41.targetText: As Jesus approached Jerusalem and saw the city, He wept over it

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending.
English names the place approached; the Greek has no object.
English joins the participle ἰδών, rendered as the finite verb saw, to approached.

19:42.sourceText: λέγων ὅτι Εἰ ἔγνως ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ταύτῃ καὶ σὺ τὰ πρὸς εἰρήνην· νῦν δὲ ἐκρύβη ἀπὸ ὀφθαλμῶν σου.
19:42.targetText: and said, “If only you had known on this day what would bring you peace! But now it is hidden from your eyes.

groups.note: The explicit subject σύ goes with had known.
πρός ("toward") in τὰ πρὸς εἰρήνην ("the things toward peace") is rendered would bring.

unmappedSource.reason: The ὅτι introducing the quotation is represented only by the quotation marks.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves καί ("even") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle λέγων, rendered as the finite verb said, to the main verb wept.
English supplies the one who would receive peace; the Greek says only "the things toward peace".

19:43.sourceText: ὅτι ἥξουσιν ἡμέραι ἐπὶ σὲ καὶ παρεμβαλοῦσιν οἱ ἐχθροί σου χάρακά σοι καὶ περικυκλώσουσίν σε καὶ συνέξουσίν σε πάντοθεν,
19:43.targetText: For the days will come upon you when your enemies will barricade you and surround you and hem you in on every side.

groups.note: The καί after "days will come" introduces what will happen in them and is rendered when.
παρεμβαλοῦσιν ... χάρακα ("will set up a barricade") is rendered will barricade.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

19:44.sourceText: καὶ ἐδαφιοῦσίν σε καὶ τὰ τέκνα σου ἐν σοί, καὶ οὐκ ἀφήσουσιν λίθον ἐπὶ λίθον ἐν σοί, ἀνθ’ ὧν οὐκ ἔγνως τὸν καιρὸν τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς σου.
19:44.targetText: They will level you to the ground—you and the children within your walls. They will not leave one stone on another, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation from God.”

groups.note: ἐδαφιοῦσιν ("will dash to the ground") is rendered will level ... to the ground.
BSB repeats the object you before adding the children.
σοί ("you"), the city, is rendered your walls.
ἀνθ’ ὧν ("in return for which") means because.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
BSB says "the children", leaving σου ("your") unexpressed; within your walls already shows whose they are.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.
BSB leaves the second ἐν σοί ("in you") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes explicit whose visitation it is; the Greek has only ἐπισκοπῆς ("visitation").

19:45.sourceText: Καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἤρξατο ἐκβάλλειν τοὺς πωλοῦντας,
19:45.targetText: Then Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were selling there.

groups.note: εἰσελθὼν εἰς ("going into") is rendered by the transitive verb entered.
The article with the participle πωλοῦντας is rendered as a relative clause.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the participle.
English joins the participle εἰσελθών, rendered as the finite verb entered, to the main verb began.
English adds a location; this verse has no Greek word for it.

19:46.sourceText: λέγων αὐτοῖς Γέγραπται Καὶ ἔσται ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς· ὑμεῖς δὲ αὐτὸν ἐποιήσατε σπήλαιον λῃστῶν.
19:46.targetText: He declared to them, “It is written: ‘My house will be a house of prayer.’ But you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the καί that opens the quotation untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

19:47.sourceText: Καὶ ἦν διδάσκων τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ· οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν ἀπολέσαι καὶ οἱ πρῶτοι τοῦ λαοῦ,
19:47.targetText: Jesus was teaching at the temple every day, but the chief priests, scribes, and leaders of the people were intent on killing Him.

groups.note: τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν ("day by day") is rendered every day.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

19:48.sourceText: καὶ οὐχ εὕρισκον τὸ τί ποιήσωσιν· ὁ λαὸς γὰρ ἅπας ἐξεκρέμετο αὐτοῦ ἀκούων.
19:48.targetText: Yet they could not find a way to do so, because all the people hung on His words.

groups.note: τὸ τί ("the what") is rendered a way.
Same verb, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The participle ἀκούων ("listening") is rendered by the idiom hung on His words.
